questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required’.

The unit twitched like a bird (preening it's plumage and becomes motionless).

options.text: preening its plumage and became motionless
preening it's plumage while becoming motionless
to preen it's plumage and becomes motionless

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'preening its plumage and became motionless ****'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence is **option 1**: *"preening its plumage and became motionless."*
 
• This sentence is discussing a past event, so the past tense verb **"became"** is more appropriate than the present tense** "becomes".**
 
• Also, **"its"** is the possessive form of** "it"**, while **"it's"** is a contraction of** "it is"** or **"it has".**
 
• **In this context,** we're talking about the bird's plumage (a possessive context), so "its" is correct.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *'The unit twitched like a bird preening its plumage and became motionless.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The other options are incorrect because:
 
 
• **Preening it's plumage while becoming motionless - **This is incorrect because it still uses the wrong form of "its/it's" and the continuous "becoming" is not as appropriate in this context.
 
 
 
• **To preen it's plumage and becomes motionless -** This is incorrect because it changes the verb tense ("to preen" instead of "preening") and it also uses the wrong form of "its/it's". The use of "becomes" is also incorrect as this is not in line with the past tense context.

 ​

सही उत्तर 'विकल्प 1' है।

**मुख्य बिंदु**

 
• दिए गए वाक्य में कोसी अंश को बदलने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प है विकल्प 1: "प्रीनिंग इट्स प्लुमेज और बिल्कुल अचल हो गया।" यह वाक्य एक पिछली घटना के बारे में बात कर रहा है, इसलिए वर्तमान काल की तुलना में अतीत काल की क्रिया "बिल्कुल अचल हो गया" अधिक उपयुक्त है। साथ ही, "इट्स" का अर्थ "यह का" होता है, जबकि "इट'स" का अर्थ "यह है" या "इसके पास है" होता है। इस संदर्भ में, हम पक्षी की प्लूमेज (एक स्वामित्व जीवन्त संदर्भ) के बारे में बात कर रहे हैं, इसलिए "इट्स" सही है। इसलिए, सही वाक्य है: 'यूनिट ने एक पक्षी की तरह हिलक्का जिसने अपनी प्लुमेज की सजावट की और बिल्कुल अचल हो गया।'

 

**अतिरिक्त जानकारी**

 
• अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि: प्रीनिंग इट'स प्लुमेज जबकि अचल हो जाता है - यह गलत है क्योंकि इसमें अभी भी "इट्स/इट'स" का गलत रूप उपयोग किया गया है और इस संदर्भ में निरंतर "बन गया" उचित नहीं है। प्लुमेज की सजावट करने और अचल हो जाने के लिए - यह गलत है क्योंकि इसने क्रिया के काल को बदल दिया ("सजावट करने" के बजाय "सजावट कर रहा") और यह भी "इट्स/इट'स" का गलत रूप उपयोग करता है। "बन गया" का उपयोग भी गलत है क्योंकि यह अतीतकालीन संदर्भ के अनुरूप नहीं है।

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

That movie is so sad; the ending always __makes me bawling__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3' **i.e.** 'makes me bawl'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct improvement for the underlined part of the sentence is option 3) **"makes me bawl."**
 
• **The original sentence,** "That movie is so sad; the ending always **makes me bawling," **is** incorrect because** the phrase **"makes me bawling"** improperly uses the progressive form of the verb "bawl" (which means to cry loudly) after "makes me."
 
• In English, the **base form of the verb** (also known as the infinitive without "to") should follow **"makes me."**

Therefore, the** correct sentence **is: "*That movie is so sad; the ending always makes me bawl."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1) "makes me bawled"** is incorrect because "bawled" is the past tense form of "bawl," which does not fit in this context.
 
• **Option 4) "made me bawl" **changes the tense of the sentence from present to past, altering the original meaning. The original sentence indicates that the movie consistently (always) has this effect, which is a present tense context.

questions.question:

__
 
• In this context, the word** "radical"** refers to those who hold extreme political or social views that are not shared by most people.(उग्र)
 
• Hence,** "fanatical"**, which means filled with excessive and single-minded zeal, especially for an extreme religious or political cause,(कट्टर) can be considered a suitable synonym.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: '**Fanatical'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Now, let's explain why other options are not suitable:
 
 
• **"Sabbatical"** is not appropriate because it typically refers to a break or a rest, often from work or academic pursuits.(विश्राम)
 
• **"Egotistical"** refers to someone who is excessively conceited or self-absorbed.(घमंडी)
 
• **"Sceptical"** suggests a tendency to doubt or question things. (उलझन)

questions.question:

options.text: will prevent the hand sanitizer of

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'** i.e. **"will prevent the hand sanitizer of".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the context of this sentence, the preposition **"of"** is incorrect.
 
• The **correct phrase** should be *"prevent the hand sanitizer from drying out your skin."*
 
• **In English,** when you want to express that you are preventing something from happening, the preposition** "from" **is used.
 
• **This is a collocation** - a common combination of words in a language - and it's simply how it's expressed in English.

Therefore, the** correct sentence **is: *"Adding aloe vera gel will prevent the hand sanitizer from drying out your skin."*

• **"Compromise, cooperation between people" -** This indicates a state of agreement reached by adjustment of conflicting or opposing claims, principles, etc., by mutual concessions.
